concerns.text: FR-019 (random‑noise baseline dataset) does not reference any User Story; it only cites SC‑003, making the requirement orphaned.
FR-020 (faithful column classification criteria) lacks a traceability link to a User Story; it only cites SC‑002, leaving it unanchored.
FR-021 (control‑perturbation dataset) is not anchored to any User Story; it only references itself (FR‑021) and FR‑007, resulting in an orphaned requirement.
FR-022 (report false‑positive/false‑negative rates) does not name a User Story; it only cites FR‑021, so it remains orphaned.

FR-001 states an explicit 80/20 train‑hold‑out split, while FR-015 uses '[deferred]' placeholders for the training and hold‑out split. These two requirements conflict: one mandates a fixed ratio, the other leaves the split undefined.
Multiple functional requirements and acceptance scenarios refer to user‑story identifiers US-1, US-2, US-3, but the spec never defines these IDs. The cross‑references are therefore unresolved.

FR-007 says the sensitivity analysis uses the control‑perturbation dataset defined in FR-022, yet FR-022 itself references the dataset defined in FR-021. The correct reference should be FR-021; the current cross‑reference is inconsistent.

SC-005 states "The computational time for the full pipeline ... is measured against an established wall‑clock time limit" but does not specify the actual time limit, making the criterion unmeasurable.
FR-021 reads "randomly permuting [deferred] of rows in each column" – the fraction to permute is left as a placeholder, so the requirement cannot be verified.
FR-015 says the dataset must be split into an [deferred] training set and a [deferred] hold‑out set; without concrete split ratios the requirement is not testable.
FR-007 depends on the control‑perturbation dataset defined in FR‑021/FR‑022; because FR‑021 is undefined, the sensitivity‑analysis step cannot be executed as specified.

FR-006 adds a multiple‑comparison correction (Benjamini‑Hochberg) which was not part of the original idea. The idea only asks for measuring fidelity; correction for multiple tests is not explicitly required and constitutes an over‑reach beyond the stated scope.

FR-007 introduces a sensitivity‑analysis sweeping significance thresholds and reporting classification stability. The original research question does not call for threshold‑sweeping or binary ‘faithful/unfaithful’ classification, so this expands the scope.

FR-014 requires generation of KDE PDFs, side‑by‑side histograms, QQ‑plots, and heatmaps as visual artifacts. The idea only demands quantitative comparison of statistical properties; visualisation requirements are not requested and add unnecessary work.

FR-018 mandates paired significance testing (t‑test or Wilcoxon) to claim overall superiority of a method. The idea does not seek a ranking or superiority claim, only a measurement of fidelity, so this is an over‑reach.

FR-019 defines a random‑noise baseline dataset for SC‑003 comparisons. The original idea never mentions a baseline; this adds a new experimental condition not required for answering the research question.

FR-020 introduces a binary ‘faithful’ vs ‘unfaithful’ column classification based on p‑value and effect‑size thresholds. The idea does not ask for binary labeling; it only asks for measuring how well distributions are reproduced.

FR-021 specifies a control‑perturbation dataset (column‑wise permutation) as a ground‑truth reference for false‑positive/false‑negative rates. This construct was not present in the idea and changes the evaluation methodology.
FR-022 requires reporting false‑positive and false‑negative rates using the control‑perturbation dataset. Since FR‑021 is itself out of scope, this downstream requirement also over‑reaches.

The spec implicitly redefines the research question from “to what extent do summary statistics, correlation structures, and distributional shapes … faithfully reproduce” to a binary classification problem with threshold‑sweeping and error‑rate reporting. This drift changes the nature of the inquiry and is not justified by the original idea.

The control‑perturbation dataset is defined by randomly permuting rows in each column, which preserves all marginal distributions while destroying all dependence structure. Using this dataset as the ground‑truth reference for both marginal‑distribution fidelity (SC‑002) and correlation fidelity (SC‑004) cannot yield meaningful false‑positive and false‑negative rates for marginal tests (all marginals will appear faithful) and for correlation tests (all correlations will appear unfaithful). This makes the validation target not independent of the predictors and renders the sensitivity analysis scientifically invalid.

Faithful classification requires (i) a Benjamini‑Hochberg‑corrected p‑value ≥ 0.05 **and** (ii) an effect‑size threshold (KS ≤ 0.1 for continuous, χ² ≤ χ²₀.₉₅ for categorical). The χ² threshold is expressed as the 95 % quantile of the χ² distribution, which is derived from the same chi‑square test that provides the p‑value. Using the same statistic to define both significance and effect size creates a circular validation: the outcome cannot be false without the test itself being satisfied, turning the claim into a tautology.

The specification mandates applying a chi‑square test to categorical marginals but does not require checking the chi‑square assumptions (e.g., expected cell counts ≥ 5). For many public tabular benchmarks, some categories are sparse, violating these assumptions and leading to inaccurate p‑values. An alternative test (e.g., Fisher’s exact test) or a pre‑check for expected counts should be specified.

The sensitivity analysis (FR‑007) sweeps significance thresholds but the fraction of rows to permute in the control‑perturbation dataset is left as a `[deferred]` placeholder in FR‑021. Without a concrete perturbation level, false‑positive and false‑negative rates (SC‑004) cannot be computed, making the claimed outcome undefined.

FR-006 adds a multiple‑comparison correction (Benjamini‑Hochberg) which was not part of the original idea. The idea only asks for measuring fidelity; correction for multiple tests is not explicitly required and constitutes an over‑reach beyond the stated scope.

FR-014 requires generation of KDE PDFs, side‑by‑side histograms, QQ‑plots, and heatmaps as visual artifacts. The idea only demands quantitative comparison of statistical properties; visualisation requirements are not requested and add unnecessary work.

FR-018 mandates paired significance testing (t‑test or Wilcoxon) to claim overall superiority of a method. The idea does not seek a ranking or superiority claim, only a measurement of fidelity, so this is an over‑reach.

The spec implicitly redefines the research question from “to what extent do summary statistics, correlation structures, and distributional shapes … faithfully reproduce” to a binary classification problem with threshold‑sweeping and error‑rate reporting. This drift changes the nature of the inquiry and is not justified by the original idea.

new_concerns.text: User Story 3 (US-3) has functional requirements (e.g., FR-008) but lacks any Success Criteria. Every user story must be backed by at least one success criterion; add one or more SCs that measure the correctness of the methodological reporting (e.g., verification that the report includes multiple‑comparison correction note and associational framing).

FR-015 still does not specify the 80/20 train‑hold‑out split required by FR-001. The current wording ('training set comprising the majority of the data and a hold‑out set comprising the remainder') leaves the ratio undefined, creating a direct conflict with FR-001 which mandates an explicit 80/20 split.
